also: the trees are losing their leaves

evidence: Cato Agr. 17: Ulmus, cum folia cadunt, tum iterum tempestīva est.
terms.comment: Cato’s plain words for the autumn fall of leaves, the same that Vergil and Horace use in their similes.

evidence: Col. 11.2: cum pampinōs ac folia dēcidere cōnsīderāssent
terms.comment: With dē-, the leaves coming off the branch.

phrases.english: The leaves are falling already: autumn is here.

phrases.latin: quam multa in silvīs autumnī frīgore prīmō lāpsa cadunt folia
phrases.english: as many as the leaves that drop and fall in the woods at the first cold of autumn

phrases.latin: Ut silvae foliīs prōnōs mūtantur in annōs, prīma cadunt
phrases.english: As the woods change their leaves as each year slides by, and the first ones fall

phrases.latin: Ulmus, cum folia cadunt, tum iterum tempestīva est.
phrases.english: The elm, when its leaves fall, is in season again (for felling).

sources: Lewis & Short: folium · Lewis & Short: cado · Lewis & Short: decido
